extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent attorneys, patent agents, and other attorneys/practitioners who represent parties before the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO)
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and related disciplinary/procedural rules for persons representing clients before the USPTO, describing duties, conflicts, recordkeeping, advertising, discipline, and related practice rules specific to patent/trademark practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent representation (§ 11.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must provide competent representation to a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with 37 CFR 11.7, competent representation in patent matters requires scientific and technical knowledge, skill, thoroughness and preparation as well as legal knowledge, skill, thoroughness and preparation; corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of representation and allocation of authority (§ 11.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the scope of representation of a client by a practitioner and allocation of authority between client and practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.2; USPTO declines to enact the ABA Model Rule 1.2(a) criminal-law-specific sentence. The lack of a specific disciplinary rule for particular conduct does not imply the conduct will not violate other USPTO Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence and promptness (§ 11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner has a duty to act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication with client (§ 11.104)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner has a duty to communicate with the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.4. Includes specific duty not to fail to timely and adequately inform a client/former client of correspondence from the Office or opponent that (i) could have a significant effect on a matter pending before the Office; (ii) is received on behalf of the client; and (iii) a reasonable practitioner would believe the client should be notified of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and fee arrangements (§ 11.105)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner responsibilities regarding fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.5. Paragraph (c) should not be construed to prohibit practitioners gaining proprietary interests in patents under § 11.108(i)(3). Paragraph (d) reserved—USPTO declines to enact criminal/domestic-relations contingent-fee rule language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of information (§ 11.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner responsibilities regarding maintaining confidentiality of information related to representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.6 but includes exceptions for inequitable conduct before the Office in addition to crimes and fraud. § 11.106(b)(3) permits disclosure to prevent, mitigate or rectify substantial injury to financial interests or property resulting from inequitable conduct before the Office. § 11.106(c) requires disclosure to the Office all information necessary to comply with duty of disclosure rules in practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent conflicts of interest (§ 11.107)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not represent a client if the representation involves a concurrent conflict of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.7; see also 37 CFR 10.66.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest for current clients: specific rules (§ 11.108)
rubrics_metrics.description: Addresses conflicts for current clients and specific rules on business transactions with clients, use of client information, gifts, literary rights, financial assistance to clients, third-party compensation, aggregate settlements, limiting liability agreements, and practitioner acquiring proprietary interest in a matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.8. § 11.108(e) prohibits financial assistance except advancing tribunal costs/expenses and for indigent clients; § 11.108(g) declines ABA criminal-law-specific portion; § 11.108(i) permits a practitioner in a patent case to take an interest in the patent as part or all of fee; § 11.108(j) reserved—USPTO declines a specific rule on sexual relations but conduct may be addressed under general provisions (e.g., § 11.804).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties to former clients (§ 11.109)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules concerning conflicts of interest and duties to former clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.9; protects former clients’ interests and sets limitations on representation adverse to former clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputation of conflicts within firm (§ 11.110)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imputation of conflicts of interest for practitioners associated in the same firm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.10; details when conflicts of one practitioner are attributable to others in the firm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successive government/private employment (§ 11.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules regarding former or current Federal Government employees who become practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO declines to enact ABA Model Rule 1.11; instead practitioner shall not engage in conduct contrary to applicable Federal ethics laws (e.g., 18 U.S.C. 207) and is subject to statutes, regulations and agency policies concerning conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputation rules for former judges/neutrals (§ 11.112)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rules regarding imputation of conflicts for practitioners who were former judges, arbitrators, mediators or third-party neutrals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.12 and sets conditions and restrictions on later practice where prior neutral service creates disqualifications or imputed conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representing organizations (§ 11.113)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner responsibilities when representing an organization as a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.13 and addresses who speaks for the organization, reporting up, and when the practitioner must withdraw or report misconduct within the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clients with diminished capacity (§ 11.114)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner responsibilities when representing a client with diminished capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.14; addresses protecting client interests while respecting client autonomy and seeking appropriate protective action when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safekeeping client property and financial records (§ 11.115)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rules regarding safekeeping of client property and maintenance of financial records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.15. § 11.115(a) requires funds kept in a separate client or third person account maintained in the state where practitioner's office is situated or elsewhere with consent; special rule for foreign practitioners. §§ 11.115(b)–(e) correspond to ABA 1.15(b)–(e). § 11.115(f) details recordkeeping requirements including cash receipts/disbursements journals, subsidiary ledgers, trial balances, handling of electronic transfers, minimum safeguards for employee access, partner responsibilities on dissolution/sale, permitted electronic/off-site storage but must be readily accessible and printable upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declining or terminating representation (§ 11.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules regarding a practitioner's responsibilities in declining or terminating representation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.16; includes withdrawal procedures and obligations especially where matters before the Office are involved (see also § 11.11(d) references to withdrawal rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Buying or selling a law practice (§ 11.117)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules regarding buying or selling a law practice or an area of law practice, including goodwill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.17. § 11.117(b) differs by proposing that where the practice or area involves patent proceedings before the Office, sale may be only to one or more registered practitioners or law firms that include at least one registered practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities to prospective clients (§ 11.118)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules regarding practitioner responsibilities to prospective clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 1.18; addresses confidentiality of information from prospective clients and conflicts arising from initial consultations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner role in providing advice (§ 11.201)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule addressing the practitioner's role in providing advice to a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 2.1. USPTO declines to enact the ABA Model Rule 2.1 last sentence limiting discussion of non-legal considerations, but notes practitioner may still refer to moral, economic, social and political factors where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluations for third parties (§ 11.203)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ethical standards where a practitioner provides an evaluation of a matter affecting a client for use by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 2.3. Practitioner must disclose evaluation information in compliance with the duty of disclosure provisions of this subchapter (see § 11.106(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serving as third-party neutral (§ 11.204)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule addressing the practitioner's role in serving as a third-party neutral (arbitrator, mediator, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 2.4 and sets duties and impartiality expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenting well-grounded positions; duty as advocate (§ 11.301)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must present well-grounded positions and use legal procedure for the fullest benefit of the client's cause but not abuse legal procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 3.1; USPTO declines to include the ABA criminal-defense-specific requirement regarding requiring every element be established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence in litigation and Office proceedings; expedite proceedings (§ 11.302)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall diligently pursue litigation and Office proceedings and make reasonable efforts to expedite proceedings before the Office as well as in litigated matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 3.2; adds explicit requirement to expedite proceedings before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of candor to tribunal; disclosure of adverse authority (§ 11.303)
rubrics_metrics.description: Continues duty of candor to a tribunal and specifies application in different situations including inter partes and ex parte proceedings before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponds to ABA Model Rule 3.3. § 11.303(a)(2) sets forth duty to disclose to the tribunal legal authority in controlling jurisdiction known to be directly adverse to client's position and not disclosed by opposing counsel in inter partes proceedings and sets forth similar duty in ex parte Office proceedings where legal authority is not otherwise disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of subordinate practitioners (§ 11.502)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner is bound by the USPTO Rules notwithstanding acting at direction of another; subordinate practitioner does not violate rules if acting in accordance with supervisory practitioner's reasonable resolution of an arguable question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subordinates are responsible for their conduct but may rely on reasonable supervisory resolutions of arguable professional duty questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities regarding non-practitioner assistants (§ 11.503)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner responsibilities concerning non-practitioner assistants employed/retained/associated with a practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partners and those with managerial/supervisory authority must make reasonable efforts to ensure measures are in effect so non-practitioner conduct is compatible with practitioner's obligations; practitioner responsible for assistant's conduct if ordered, ratified, or if practitioner has managerial authority and fails to take remedial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional independence of a practitioner (§ 11.504)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibitions on sharing legal fees with non-practitioners, partnerships with non-practitioners, and allowing non-practitioners to direct professional judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited exceptions (e.g., post-death payments, purchase of deceased's practice, inclusion of employees in compensation plans, sharing fees with qualified nonprofit organizations). Prohibits non-practitioner ownership/control of law firm that would affect professional judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unauthorized practice of law (§ 11.505)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not practice law in a jurisdiction in violation of that jurisdiction's regulation nor assist others in unauthorized practice before the Office or elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes prohibitions on aiding suspended/disbarred/excluded practitioners in unauthorized practice and restrictions on patent-agent-only individuals practicing trademark matters in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on right to practice (§ 11.506)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner shall not participate in agreements that restrict a practitioner's right to practice after termination of the relationship, except retirement benefit agreements, nor agree to restrictions as part of client controversy settlements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits post-termination practice restrictions that impede professional autonomy except limited exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities regarding law-related services (§ 11.507)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner subject to USPTO Rules with respect to provision of law-related services when such services are not distinct from legal services or when practitioner-controlled entities provide such services without adequate disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If law-related services are provided in circumstances not distinct from legal services, practitioner must comply with USPTO Rules; if practitioner fails to take reasonable measures to assure clients know services are not legal, USPTO Rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications concerning a practitioner's services (§ 11.701)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not make a false or misleading communication about the practitioner or the practitioner's services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A communication is false or misleading if it contains a material misrepresentation of fact or law, or omits a fact necessary to make the statement as a whole not materially misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising (§ 11.702)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for advertising legal services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subject to §§ 11.701 and 11.703, practitioners may advertise through written, recorded or electronic communication including public media. Practitioners shall not give anything of value for recommending services except limited exceptions (e.g., paying reasonable cost of advertising, reciprocal referral agreements that are non-exclusive and disclosed). Communications must include the name and office address of at least one practitioner or law firm responsible for content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct contact with prospective clients / solicitation (§ 11.703)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on in-person, telephone or real-time electronic solicitation of professional employment for pecuniary gain and related labeling requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits live-solicitation when significant motive is pecuniary gain unless recipient is a practitioner or has family/close personal/prior professional relationship. Prohibits solicitation by written/recorded/electronic means if recipient has told practitioner not to solicit or if solicitation involves coercion/duress/harassment. Solicitation communications to persons known to need legal services must include 'Advertising Material' on envelope and at beginning/ending of recordings, unless recipient is exempt. Prepaid/group legal service plans may use in-person/telephone contact under specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of fields of practice and specialization (§ 11.704)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on stating areas of practice and specialty designations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner may state fields of law practiced. Registered patent practitioner who is an attorney may use 'Patents', 'Patent Attorney', etc.; registered patent agent (non-attorney) may use 'Patent Agent', etc., but patent agents generally may not hold out as authorized to practice trademark matters or before a court. Practitioner may not claim certification as a specialist unless certified by an organization approved by an appropriate state authority or ABA-accredited and certifying organization's name is identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm names and letterheads (§ 11.705)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on firm names, letterheads and trade names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Firm names/letterheads must not violate § 11.701; trade names may be used if they do not imply government connection or violate § 11.701. Name of practitioner holding public office shall not be used in firm name or communications during substantial period when not actively practicing with the firm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration, recognition and disciplinary matters (§ 11.801)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibitions related to applications and disciplinary/reinstatement matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants or practitioners shall not knowingly make false statements of material fact, fail to disclose facts necessary to correct a misapprehension, knowingly fail to respond to lawful demands for information (subject to § 11.106 confidentiality), or fail to cooperate with OED in investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial and legal officials (§ 11.802)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions on statements about judges and public legal officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner shall not knowingly make false or reckless statements concerning qualifications or integrity of a judge, adjudicatory officer or public legal officer or candidate for such office. Practitioner-candidates for judicial office must comply with applicable Code of Judicial Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting professional misconduct (§ 11.803)
rubrics_metrics.description: Duty to report misconduct by other practitioners or judicial/legal officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner who knows another practitioner has committed a violation raising a substantial question as to honesty, trustworthiness or fitness shall inform the OED Director and other appropriate authority. Also requires reporting judicial misconduct raising substantial fitness questions. Does not require disclosure of information protected by § 11.106 or obtained in approved lawyers assistance programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misconduct—definitions and examples (§ 11.804)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerates professional misconduct prohibited by the USPTO Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Professional misconduct includes violating/attempting to violate the USPTO Rules (or assisting/inducing others), committing criminal acts reflecting adversely on honesty/fitness, engaging in dishonesty/fraud/deceit/misrepresentation, conduct prejudicial to administration of justice, implying ability to improperly influence government agencies or officials, knowingly assisting judges or Office officers in violations, being publicly disciplined by State/US/foreign authority, or other conduct reflecting adversely on fitness to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Savings clause for prior conduct (§ 11.901)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposition of disciplinary proceedings relating to conduct occurring before effective date of these regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings based on conduct before the effective date may be instituted if such conduct would continue to justify sanctions under these provisions; no practitioner subject to discipline for conduct that would not have been disciplinable before the effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (§ 41.5(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Counsel may not withdraw from a proceeding before the Board unless the Board authorizes such withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-references § 11.116 regarding conditions for withdrawal; withdrawal requires Board authorization.
